## Summary

Universal Global Scientific Industrial is the Taiwan company of the USI electronics manufacturing group, set up in 2010, the same year the original Universal Scientific Industrial Co., Ltd. (founded 1976) was delisted from the Taiwan Stock Exchange [5]. An SEC filing describes it as a Republic of China corporation that holds Universal Scientific Industrial Co., Ltd. as a subsidiary [2]. USI says it is a subsidiary of ASE Technology Holding [3], and the Taipei Times calls the group's Shanghai company, Universal Scientific Industrial (Shanghai), a unit of ASE Group that makes Wi-Fi modules for products such as Apple's iPhone [4]. The IEEE registry gives this name 23 MA-L blocks at Tsao Tuen, Nantou addresses [1].

USI has made Wi-Fi and Bluetooth modules since 2003 and WWAN modules since 2008 [5]. A MAC in these blocks is therefore usually a module inside another brand's product rather than a USI-branded device. DeviWiki lists USI-built access points and routers for Meru Networks (Broadcom BCM43460 in the AP832), USRobotics (Broadcom BCM5350 in the USR5432, BCM5354 in the USR5455), Proxim (Atheros AR5312A) and the TonidoPlug 2 NAS (Marvell 88F6283 with 88W8786), plus USI modules on Broadcom, Cypress and Marvell silicon, with FCC grantee codes IXM and COF [6].

Randomization depends on the host product and is not documented. No security advisory naming USI was found.
